Counterpart is the string duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld uses for its own 1735 gain; the reviewer's alternative duchy-of-saxe-gotha-altenburg (a 1735/8 stand-in loss) is not used because the page says 'von Sachsen-Coburg' and no page opened gives Gotha these districts. duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld has no matching loss to saxe-meiningen (its owner should add one). region.text: the state's outline as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918

ledger.note: November 1918: the duchy ends in the German Revolution. The page gives the year only ('Dukedom abolished in 1918'; infobox 'German Revolution: 1918'): 'Duke Bernhard III, brother-in-law of Emperor Wilhelm II, was forced to abdicate'; 'The succeeding Free State of Saxe-Meiningen became part of the new state of Thuringia on 1 May 1920.' The month rests on the revolution page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed' (German revolution of 1918-1919 page). Infobox status 'Constituent state of the German Empire (1871-1918)'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

notes:
Written for batch eu-20-l (5 pages; budget up to 5). The Cliopatria row 'Saxe-Meiningen' (1820-1870) has seven shapes.

CLIOPATRIA ROW MIX-UP. The 1836-1839 shape is the old 1820 outline of Meiningen alone (wrong, no page shows Meiningen losing land), while the Cliopatria row 'Saxe-Coburg and Gotha' (1836-1839) holds nine cells of the Hildburghausen/Saalfeld land inside Meiningen's 1828 shape plus Sonneberg and Coburg. The saxe-coburg-and-gotha dossier corrects that side. The 1828 shape also holds Rudolstadt, Gehren and Ilmenau (Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt land: Cliopatria has no row for that principality; a dossier is needed) and omits Sonneberg and the exclaves of Camburg and Kranichfeld, which the English page names among the 1868 Kreise. Areas: 3,294 km2 against about 2,400 (German page) and 2,468 (1910, English page).

DATES. The Cliopatria shape begins in 1828; the pages give 12 November 1826 (arbitration of the King of Saxony; Saxe-Hildburghausen page infobox 'Passed to Saxe-Meiningen: 1826'). The change of the area in 1866 (3,294 to 3,206) and 1868 (3,206 to 3,184) is invisible at the grid (identical cells); the only 1866 transfer on the pages is the village of Abtlöbnitz near Camburg (8 October 1866), direction not stated, entered as a loss to kingdom-of-prussia in the repair below.

NOT SETTLED. (1) 1680-1728: no page dates a border change; the keyframe uses Cliopatria's 1820 shape (the 1729-1753 acquisitions are in the repair below). (2) Camburg's previous holder is not on any page; Gotha-Altenburg is a reading (confidence 2). (3) End year 1871 follows the sibling dossiers; the monarchy ended in November 1918 (Free State of Saxe-Meiningen 1918-1920, then Thuringia on 1 May 1920). (4) The 1867 membership of the North German Confederation is not territorial and not entered.
